page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is a high-density compute server powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 288 vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64 and includes a 504 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1080 GB of RAM, providing approximately 3.75 GB of memory per core. Storage is bundled, consisting of 48 local NVMe SSDs totaling 19,031 GB of local storage capacity. No GPUs are present on this instance.

In benchmark testing, this server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% on stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. The Intel Xeon processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to top-tier scores in extended instructions, cryptography, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached small-block reads reaching 22,949.13 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 1,062.88 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top 10%, alongside static web serving throughput. However, single-core CPU performance and certain text generation tasks for small LLM models fall into average or lower tiers.

Given its massive core count and integrated high-capacity NVMe SSD storage, this server offers high resource density for workloads requiring simultaneous compute and fast local I/O. The qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the consolidation of massive compute power and local storage, reducing the need for external storage attachments. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd is a high-density compute server featuring 288 vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor, 1080 GB of RAM, and 19,031 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 48 drives. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 144 physical cores and hyper-threading, it delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance and exceptional memory bandwidth. The processor supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX, driving strong results in encryption, database operations, and ray tracing. While single-core performance is average, its massive parallel processing capabilities and integrated high-speed storage make it highly efficient for demanding workloads. It is best suited for large-scale database operations, software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing.
